name: pixel streaming and cloud game streaming platforms
title: Best Pixel Streaming and Cloud Game Streaming Platforms for Studios in 2026
summary_line: Pixel streaming platforms host your Unreal, Unity or Windows build on cloud GPUs and deliver it to browsers; this list compares studio-facing options.
definition: Pixel streaming runs a game or real-time 3D application on a GPU server and sends the rendered video to a browser or device, so viewers need no download or powerful hardware. Studios use it for playable demos, product configurators, trade-show builds and cloud game launches. Platforms differ in engine support, billing and how much infrastructure you operate yourself.
intro: A studio that wants players, publishers or clients to try a build without installing it has three routes: rent GPU time and wire up streaming yourself, buy a managed pixel streaming service, or run a cloud game platform at scale. This list covers all three, so the order reflects how quickly a small team can go from a packaged build to a shareable link. We read vendor home pages, pricing pages and About pages on the day of review and did not run load or latency tests. Prices appear only where a vendor published them; several enterprise vendors show none, and we say so. Engine coverage, billing style and how much operations work you inherit decide the position of each entry. Vendors that could not be opened, including Arcware and Furioos, are left out rather than described from memory.

criteria.heading: Engine and build support
criteria.text: Confirm the engine before anything else. Eagle 3D Streaming and Streampixel center on Unreal Engine, PureWeb names Unreal Engine and Unity, and Vagon streams applications from a cloud computer. A generic GPU cloud such as CoreWeave or Paperspace can run anything you can containerize, but you build the streaming layer yourself. Ask whether a plain Windows .exe is accepted, because many demo builds are not packaged for a specific engine plugin.

criteria.heading: Billing shape for demos
criteria.text: Demos are bursty, so how a vendor meters concurrency matters more than the headline rate. Streampixel charges a flat EUR 99 per month with 2 concurrent users and EUR 45 per extra concurrent user. Vagon bills by the minute from $0.25 per hour. Edgegap says per minute with no fixed monthly fee. Eagle 3D Streaming offers a free trial, and CoreWeave lists hourly GPU prices. Estimate peak simultaneous viewers, not total viewers.

criteria.heading: Operations you inherit
criteria.text: Managed services hide GPU orchestration; infrastructure providers do not. Streampixel says it runs its own data centers, and PureWeb positions itself as a platform for distributing apps. Paperspace and CoreWeave sell compute and leave scaling, session handling and security to you. Amazon GameLift Streams is a managed AWS service, though its overview page gave little readable detail. Count the engineer-weeks you would spend, not only the monthly bill.

criteria.heading: Delivery and branding controls
criteria.text: A shareable link is not the same as an embeddable, branded experience. Check for custom loading screens, CI/CD hooks, analytics and security controls. Streampixel lists custom splash screens, a source control connection and real-time analytics. Others did not publish these details in the text we read. If clients will see the stream, also confirm browser coverage on phones and whether end users need any GPU of their own; Eagle 3D Streaming says they do not need a high-end one.

market_notes: Counting the ten entries: three publish usable prices (Streampixel, Vagon and CoreWeave), two more describe billing style without amounts (Edgegap and Paperspace), and the rest give no price in the text we read. Streampixel and Vagon are the only entries with a stated trial price or length, and Eagle 3D Streaming also advertises a free trial. Engine-specific services cluster around Unreal; only PureWeb names Unity among the managed options.

The practical trade-off is control versus speed. A managed service gets a link online in an afternoon but ties you to its engine support and its concurrency pricing. A GPU cloud gives you control and a lower unit cost at scale, but you carry orchestration and security work. Vendor origin varies: Streampixel's operator is Estonian, Ubitus operates from Taipei, Tokyo and Malaysia, and CoreWeave was founded in New Jersey; most other pages named no country.

how_to_choose.title: Package one build first
how_to_choose.text: Export the exact build you want to show, with its launcher, config files and any required runtime. Check whether each vendor takes a packaged Unreal build, an .exe or a container. Streampixel describes uploading a packaged build or .exe, and Eagle 3D Streaming describes Unreal Engine 5 applications. A build that fails on the vendor's trial machine tells you more than any feature table.

how_to_choose.title: Model your peak concurrency
how_to_choose.text: Write down how many people will be in the demo at the same moment: a launch day, a conference hour, a publisher call. Compare that with included concurrent sessions, such as the 2 in Streampixel's plan, or per-minute metering at Vagon or Edgegap. Include the cost of failing a live demo, because overage and queue rules differ between vendors.

how_to_choose.title: Decide who runs the servers
how_to_choose.text: If nobody on your team wants to manage GPUs, rank managed services above infrastructure. If you already run cloud workloads, CoreWeave, Paperspace or Amazon GameLift Streams may cost less over a year. Ask each vendor about uptime reporting and support channels, and keep a fallback such as a recorded video for the first live event.

faqs.q: What is the best pixel streaming platform for studios in 2026?
faqs.a: Eagle 3D Streaming is the best starting point for a small studio because it streams Unreal Engine 5 builds to any browser and advertises a free trial with no credit card. Streampixel is better if you want a flat monthly price, and PureWeb is better if your build uses Unity as well as Unreal.

faqs.q: Can I stream a Unity game, not only Unreal?
faqs.a: PureWeb states that it distributes Unreal Engine and Unity apps through Pixel Streaming and Render Streaming. Eagle 3D Streaming and Streampixel are described around Unreal Engine. Vagon runs applications on a cloud computer, and GPU clouds such as CoreWeave can run a Unity build if you set up the streaming layer yourself.

faqs.q: How much does pixel streaming cost?
faqs.a: It varies by model. Streampixel lists EUR 99 per month with unlimited minutes and 2 concurrent users, Vagon bills by the minute from $0.25 per hour, and CoreWeave lists hourly GPU rates. PureWeb, Ubitus and Amazon GameLift Streams showed no plan amounts in the text we read, so request quotes.

faqs.q: Do viewers need a powerful PC?
faqs.a: No, that is the point of the approach. Eagle 3D Streaming says end users do not need a high-end GPU, and Streampixel delivers builds in the browser through a share link. Viewers do need a stable connection, and the vendors publish few minimum bandwidth figures.

faqs.q: Is a cloud PC the same as pixel streaming?
faqs.a: Not quite. A cloud PC such as Vagon or Shadow gives a remote Windows machine you can stream from, while pixel streaming platforms are built to publish a specific application to many viewers with a link and session management. Cloud PCs suit small private demos and creative work.

faqs.q: Do I need a game server platform too?
faqs.a: Only for multiplayer. Pixel streaming renders one session per viewer, while a service such as Edgegap orchestrates dedicated game servers and also lists cloud gaming among its uses. Many studios use streaming for demos and orchestration for the live game.

faqs.q: Which vendors publish company or location details?
faqs.a: Streampixel's footer names Vardexa OÜ and its price is in euros. Ubitus says it was founded in 2012 with operations in Taipei, Tokyo and Malaysia. CoreWeave says it was founded in 2017 in New Jersey. Paperspace names its entity as Paperspace dba DigitalOcean. Most others gave no company details.

tools.name: Eagle 3D Streaming
tools.tagline: Unreal Engine 5 streaming to any browser
tools.pricing: Free trial with no credit card; a plan starts free before scaling with Core, and annual billing includes 2 free months.
tools.platforms: Any web browser; end users do not need a high-end GPU
features: Annual billing with two free months
tools.summary: It streams Unreal Engine 5 apps to any browser, needs no end-user GPU and offers a free trial with no credit card.
tools.verdict: Eagle 3D Streaming comes first for a studio testing the idea. The home page says users can stream Unreal Engine 5 applications to any web browser and that end users do not need a high-end GPU. The pricing page offers a free trial with no credit card and a plan that begins free before moving to Core, with annual billing that includes 2 free months. That path lets a team validate a demo before paying.
tools.weaknesses: The pricing amounts for the Core plan were not in the text we read, the company and country were not captured, and the pages stress Unreal Engine 5 rather than Unity or other engines.
tools.wrong_for: Skip it if your build is Unity-first; PureWeb names Unity support. Teams wanting a fixed, published monthly figure may prefer Streampixel.

sources.fact: Eagle 3D Streaming lets users stream Unreal Engine 5 applications to any web browser.
The home page says end users do not need a high-end GPU.
The pricing page offers a free trial with no credit card required and a plan that starts free before scaling with Core.

tools.name: Streampixel
tools.tagline: Flat-rate Unreal pixel streaming in the browser
tools.pricing: EUR 99 per month with unlimited minutes and 2 concurrent users; EUR 45 per month per extra concurrent user; 2-day free trial.
tools.platforms: Browser delivery of Unreal Engine builds
tools.summary: One flat EUR 99 monthly plan with unlimited minutes and 2 concurrent users, plus a 2-day free trial.
tools.verdict: Streampixel is second because its pricing is the easiest to forecast. You upload a packaged Unreal build or .exe, receive a share link and pay EUR 99 per month, with 2 concurrent users included and EUR 45 per month for each extra concurrent user. Features listed include 4K streaming, custom splash screens, a CI/CD source control connection, analytics and security controls. The vendor says it runs RTX 6000 Ada GPUs in its own data centers.
tools.weaknesses: Concurrency is the constraint: 2 sessions are included, so a busy launch costs more. It is built for Unreal Engine and the trial lasts two days. Performance claims are the vendor's own.
tools.wrong_for: Avoid it if you need Unity streaming or per-minute billing for rare demos; PureWeb or Vagon fit those cases better.

sources.fact: Streampixel runs Unreal Engine applications in the browser on RTX GPUs; users upload a packaged build or .exe and get a share link.
Pricing is a flat EUR 99 per month with unlimited minutes and 2 concurrent users; additional concurrent capacity costs EUR 45 per month per CCU.
Included features list 4K streaming, a source control connection for CI/CD, custom splash screens, security controls, analytics and built-in voice, video and text chat.

tools.wrong_for: Skip it if you need a visible price or a self-serve free trial today; Eagle 3D Streaming and Streampixel publish both. Raw GPU control points to CoreWeave.

tools.name: Amazon GameLift Streams
tools.pricing: The overview page has a Pricing section and links to AWS Pricing; plan amounts are not in the extracted text.
tools.summary: A managed streaming service on AWS, useful if your team already holds an AWS account and billing relationship.
tools.verdict: Amazon GameLift Streams is fourth because it fits a specific buyer. The AWS overview page identifies it as a game streaming service, with a Pricing section linking to AWS Pricing and the Pricing Calculator. Studios that already use AWS for backend, identity and billing can add streaming without a new vendor. It is the most conventional enterprise route here.
tools.weaknesses: The extracted page was mostly AWS navigation, so features and prices could not be read in detail. We cannot confirm engine coverage or limits from the text we saw, so check AWS documentation yourself.
tools.wrong_for: Avoid it if you want a quick shareable demo link without cloud setup; Streampixel or Eagle 3D Streaming are quicker. Studios off AWS should compare CoreWeave.
